setup: Stand perpendicular to a sturdy wall or doorframe in a comfortable staggered stance.
Place your palm and forearm flat against the wall at roughly shoulder height, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
steps: Gently rotate your torso and hips away from the braced arm until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest and the front of your shoulder.
Hold the position steadily without bouncing or aggressively twisting.
Slowly rotate your torso back toward the wall to release the tension, then switch sides.
instructions.breathing: Breathe deeply and evenly, allowing the chest musculature to relax further with each exhale.
cues: Rotate gently from the hips and torso

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulder toward the ear on the stretched side.
common_faults.correction: Keep the shoulder blade depressed and drawn slightly backward before turning away.

common_faults.fault: Over-rotating through the lower back instead of the upper torso.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a braced core and turn your entire rib cage and hips smoothly as a unit.

common_faults.fault: Aggressively forcing the shoulder into hyper-horizontal abduction.
common_faults.correction: Ease into the stretch until a mild to moderate pull is felt; never push into sharp joint pain.

precautions: Avoid this stretch if you experience anterior shoulder instability or impingement symptoms.

name: Wall Chest Stretch
summary: A standing static stretch performed by bracing the hand or forearm against a wall and rotating the torso away to stretch the chest and front shoulder.
